First judge whether you are willing to work in a composites workshop according to ratios and process parameters over the long term, accept standing and repetitive motions and wear protective equipment, and carry out ventilation, curing and inspection according to the procedures; verify with this page's paper exercises and the seven-day task.

The daily work of fiberglass laminators and fabricators revolves around the process of "mold—layup—cure—trim—inspect": before starting, inspect, clean and assemble the mold and apply mold release wax and varnish to the mold surface; mix catalyst into resin according to the ratio and saturate fiber cloth and fiber mat with a brush; select and cut pre-cut fiber mat, fiber cloth and wooden reinforcement materials according to the project; lay the saturated fiber layers onto the mold by hand or with a squeegee and use rollers to remove air bubbles and flatten seams; repeatedly apply resin layers to the mold surface until the required thickness is reached and wait for gelling; complete curing by leaving it at room temperature, using heat lamps or an oven; trim excess material with hand shears or a trim knife and, where necessary, saw cured parts with a diamond cutting blade; measure with a ruler or micrometer and inspect visually and by tapping to check whether the finished part meets specifications and has no bubbles or voids; inspect and repair damaged or nonconforming fiberglass parts; mask areas that are not to be laminated and verify that the mold, templates and cutting templates match the drawings or customer specifications. A pneumatic spray gun with a chopper attachment may also be used to spray chopped fiberglass, resin and catalyst onto a prepared mold; the actual ratios, curing and equipment operation follow the verified process, and parameters are not taken from an occupational overview.

Work context｜Fiberglass laminators and fabricators work in composites workshops, shipyards and manufacturing sites, forming a production cycle around mold preparation, resin saturation, layup and rolling, curing and thickness control, trimming and cutting, and inspection and repair.
Work locations｜Boat and yacht yards, automobile and specialty vehicle plants, wind power and storage tank manufacturing workshops, sports and amusement equipment plants, and composite part processing and repair workshops.
Working conditions｜Mainly standing and manual work ("standing continually or almost continually" 97%, "bending or twisting the body continually or almost continually" 53%, "making repetitive motions continually or almost continually" 37%, with another 48% more than half the time, in O*NET work context); daily exposure to contaminants 76%; work schedules are mainly fixed shifts (62%) with 36% irregular; 34% of respondents work more than 40 hours per week; the work requires a high degree of exactness and accuracy (extremely important 33%, very important 35%); the consequence of error is extremely serious (22%) or very serious (23%).
Main objects｜Fiberglass mat and cloth, resin and catalyst, mold release wax and varnish, wooden reinforcement materials, molds and templates, cutting and sanding tools, and process parameters and inspection records.
Collaboration｜Working with the crew leader or process technician, colleagues, quality inspectors, mold and material suppliers, and design and customer representatives.

Tools and materials｜Rollers and brushes, squeegees and hand shears, trim knives and diamond cutting blades, pneumatic spray equipment (with a chopper attachment), mixing and weighing utensils, heat lamps or ovens, ventilation and protective equipment, and drawings, specifications and process parameter sheets.

Record requirements｜Resin and catalyst ratio records, layup and thickness records, curing temperature and time records, inspection and repair records, and ventilation and protective equipment check records must be documented according to employer rules.

entries.answer: Lay up layers of fiberglass and resin on molds to make fiberglass reinforced plastic products such as hulls and decks and golf cart and automobile bodies: inspect, clean and assemble the mold and apply mold release wax and varnish; mix catalyst into resin and saturate fiber cloth and fiber mat with a brush; select and cut fiber mat, fiber cloth and wooden reinforcement materials; lay the saturated fiber layers by hand or with a squeegee and use rollers to remove air bubbles and flatten seams; repeatedly apply resin layers to the required thickness; cure at room temperature or with heat lamps or an oven; trim with hand shears, a trim knife or a diamond cutting blade; and measure, inspect visually and by tapping and repair defects according to specifications.
entries.question: What do fiberglass laminators and fabricators mainly do?

entries.answer: The objects of responsibility differ: this occupation mainly laminates fiberglass and resin on molds and completes curing, trimming and inspection; extruding and forming machine setters, operators and tenders for synthetic and glass fibers mainly operate extrusion and forming equipment; molders and casting workers mainly make molds and castings; assemblers and fabricators mainly assemble components; aircraft structure assemblers mainly assemble aircraft structures and install systems; mechanical insulators mainly install insulation on pipes and equipment; glass blowers and molders mainly form glass; and first-line production supervisors are responsible for assigning tasks and supervising production quality and safety.

entries.answer: O*NET lists this occupation as Job Zone 1–2 (little to some preparation), SVP below 6.0; in the education survey about 46% indicated that a high school diploma or equivalent is needed, 43% indicated below a high school diploma and 11% indicated some college education but no degree. Related occupational training usually requires a high school or GED credential, with pre-employment training ranging from a few days to one year. Work involving resin and catalyst requires chemical safety and protection training according to local requirements and good ventilation and protection; process parameter adjustment and quality judgment usually require post training and experience. In mainland China, manufacturing post training plus practice is commonly required, and the specifics are subject to recruitment announcements and local provisions.

entries.answer: A more accurate judgment is that some tasks will be assisted by tools and that the occupation as a whole will mainly see augmentation and structural adjustment. A 2023 ILO study shows that task exposure varies widely across occupations and that technical feasibility does not mean workshops have already adopted it; meanwhile ratio execution, layup and rolling, curing judgment and appearance and tap inspection require hand feel and experience, and chemical and dust protection also requires on-site judgment, so the conclusion is that the way of working will change rather than that the occupation as a whole will be replaced.

entries.answer: No. The median is the midpoint of the wage distribution of practitioners within the same statistical period, not a starting salary. Schedules for this occupation are mainly fixed shifts with 36% irregular arrangements, and some workshops price by piece rate or per batch; personal income must be judged together with the pay method (hourly, piece rate or per batch) and actual hours (O*NET work context shows 34% of respondents work more than 40 hours per week).

entries.answer: Yes. Related occupational training shows that pre-employment training for this occupation ranges from a few days to one year, and most posts are taken up through mentoring. However, posts involving resin, catalyst and dust work usually require chemical safety and protection training and must provide ventilation and protection according to safety data sheets and occupational health requirements; process parameter adjustment and quality judgment generally require post training and experience. Whether it is feasible depends on the target employer and local provisions, and this page does not replace the original regulations and does not provide chemical safety or occupational health advice.
